A1.justification: Despite the title change, both PDFs describe the same optimized linear measurement research. All pages, including figures, equations, Table 1, and appendices A–F, are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original two-dimensional simulations, MNIST and CelebA reconstruction experiments, measurement-statistics analyses, and perceptual-loss results in Figures 1–5 and Table 1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds experiments on sequential measurements, measurement noise, and sampling-parameter sensitivity.

M1.justification: The original joint measurement optimization and denoiser-based reconstruction remain. v3 adds two adaptations: greedy sequential construction of OLMseq in Appendix E.6, and OLMnoise obtained by injecting measurement noise during optimization in Section 3.4.

E1.justification: The synthetic distributions, MNIST, and CelebA remain unchanged. Figure 4H adds Gaussian-corrupted linear measurements as a MNIST test scenario, extending evaluation beyond the previously noise-free measurements.

E2.justification: New Figure 4G–H compares standard OLM with the added OLMseq and OLMnoise variants. The existing PCA, random-measurement, ICA, and Table 1 comparisons remain; Wu et al. (2019) becomes Wu et al. (2019b), representing the same comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include measurement-noise testing on MNIST at k = 32, optimization with noise standard deviation 0.4, and sampler-parameter and averaging-count sweeps. Figure 4E switches from signed to absolute skewness. Existing splits, training budgets, and two-sample optimization/sixteen-sample evaluation defaults are retained.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostics through sequential-constraint and noise-robustness experiments in Figure 4G–H and four sensitivity plots covering step size, injected noise, stopping criterion, and sample averaging in Supplementary Figure 1. Section 3.5 also adds a comparison of subspaces optimized for different losses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Table 1's standard-error reporting. No independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added. The new conditional-sample averaging sweep measures reconstruction accuracy rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figure 3's peak advantages of 4.72 dB on MNIST and 0.44 dB on CelebA, and all Table 1 values, are retained. New results report a small sequential-ordering penalty, improved high-noise robustness with a low-noise tradeoff, and diminishing gains from sample averaging. Section 3.5 newly reports lower PSNR for SSIM optimization than for PCs.

T1.justification: Appendix E.6 adds the constrained sequential formulation: a new measurement parameterized by a unit coefficient vector in the remaining orthogonal subspace, an appended measurement matrix, and Equation (17). The existing Tweedie/Miyasawa and PCA proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain learning dataset- and loss-dependent linear measurements through denoiser priors, improving reconstruction over conventional measurements, and identifying asymmetric measurement distributions. The title changes from Optimal to Generalized without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the inference that random measurements underperform because sparse priors inadequately describe the images. It adds sequential-ordering, noise-robustness, and SSIM–PSNR tradeoffs, while acknowledging that fuller noise analysis needs a suitable reconstruction algorithm. It also removes v2's explicit nonconvex-optimality caveat.

D1.justification: v3 documents variant settings, including sequential initialization at k = 1 and measurement-noise standard deviation 0.4. Appendix E revises the rationale for using two optimization samples and identifies iterative U-Net backpropagation as the computational bottleneck. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, time estimates, and code access remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on diffusion inverse problems, measurement learning, and task-specific dimensionality reduction, including Wang et al. (2022), Li and Zhang et al. (2024), Wu et al. (2019a), and Pineda et al. (2020). It removes the end-to-end image-compression reference by Ballé et al. (2016), while retaining the principal research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, updates publication and author metadata, and edits the introduction, method explanations, result descriptions, and conclusion. Appendix E.6 is added, but the main section order and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 gains panels G–H and revised skewness and mutual-information displays. A new four-panel Supplementary Figure 1 is inserted, with existing supplementary figures renumbered 2–4. Legends, captions, and publication headers also change; most existing displays and Table 1's structure are retained.

improvement.justification: The added constraint, noise-robustness, and sampler-sensitivity experiments better support practical choices and limitations left unexplored in v2. The SSIM–PSNR tradeoff is also clearer. These are useful but limited extensions: core benchmark results remain unchanged and realistic noisy reconstruction remains unresolved. Removing the nonconvex-optimality caveat loses a qualification, but the added evidence supports a modest net improvement.
